# Judges Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_285.jpg, JDG_page_286.jpg

1. And Shimshon went to Azzah, and he saw there a prostitute woman, and he went in to her.

2. [It was told] to the Azzathites, saying, "Shimshon has come here." And they surrounded [him] and lay in wait for him all night at the gate of the city. And they were quiet all night, saying, "Until the light of morning, then we will kill him."

3. And Shimshon lay until the middle of the night. And he arose at the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and he pulled them up with the bar, and he put [them] on his shoulders and carried them up to the top of the mountain that [is] before Chevron.

4. And it was after this, he loved a woman in the Valley of Soreq, and her name [was] D'lilah.

5. And the lords of the P'lishtim went up to her and said to her, "Entice him and see in what [his] great strength [is], and how we can overpower him, and we will bind him to afflict him. And we — each of us — will give you eleven hundred [pieces] of silver."

6. And D'lilah said to Shimshon, "Tell me, I pray, in what [is] your great strength, and with what you could be bound to afflict you."

7. And Shimshon said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I shall become weak and be like any [other] man."

8. And the lords of the P'lishtim brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

9. And the ambush was sitting for her in the inner chamber. And she said to him, "The P'lishtim [are] upon you, Shimshon!" And he snapped the bowstrings as a strand of tow snaps when it touches fire. And his strength was not known.

10. And D'lilah said to Shimshon, "Behold, you have mocked me and told me lies. Now tell me, I pray, with what you could be bound."

11. And he said to her, "If they surely bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, I shall become weak and be like any [other] man."

12. And D'lilah took new ropes and bound him with them and said to him, "The P'lishtim [are] upon you, Shimshon!" And the ambush was sitting in the inner chamber. And he snapped them from upon his arms like a thread.

13. And D'lilah said to Shimshon, "Until now you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with what you could be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven locks of my head with the web."

14. And she fastened [it] with the pin and said to him, "The P'lishtim [are] upon you, Shimshon!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled up the pin of the loom and the web.

15. And she said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart [is] not with me? Three times you have mocked me and have not told me in what [is] your great strength."

16. And it was, when she pressed him with her words all the days and urged him, his soul was shortened to death.

17. And he told her all his heart and said to her, "A razor has not gone up upon my head, for a Nazirite of God I [have been] from the womb of my mother. If I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I shall become weak and be like any [other] man."

18. And D'lilah saw that he had told her all his heart. And she sent and called the lords of the P'lishtim, saying, "Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart." And the lords of the P'lishtim came up to her and brought up the silver in their hand.

19. And she made him sleep upon her knees. And she called the man and had him shave off the seven locks of his head. And she began to afflict him, and his strength departed from him.

20. And she said, "The P'lishtim [are] upon you, Shimshon!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times and shake myself free." And he did not know that YHWH had departed from him.

21. And the P'lishtim seized him and gouged out his eyes. And they brought him down to Azzah and bound him with bronze [chains]. And he was grinding in the prison house.

22. And the hair of his head began to grow after it was shaved.

23. And the lords of the P'lishtim gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice. And they said, "Our god has given Shimshon our enemy into our hand."

24. And the people saw him and praised their god, for they said, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy and the destroyer of our land, who multiplied our slain."

25. And it was, when their heart was merry, they said, "Call Shimshon and let him amuse us." And they called Shimshon from the prison house, and he amused before them. And they stood him between the pillars.

26. And Shimshon said to the youth who held his hand, "Let me feel the pillars on which the house rests, and let me lean on them."

27. And the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the P'lishtim [were] there. And on the roof [were] about three thousand men and women watching the amusement of Shimshon.

28. And Shimshon called to YHWH and said, "Lord YHWH, remember me, I pray, and strengthen me, I pray, only this once, O God, and let me be avenged [with] one vengeance for my two eyes from the P'lishtim."

29. And Shimshon grasped the two middle pillars on which the house rested and leaned on them — one with his right [hand] and one with his left.

30. And Shimshon said, "Let my soul die with the P'lishtim." And he bent with strength, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people who [were] in it. And the dead whom he killed at his death were more than those he killed in his life.

31. And his brothers and all the house of his father went down and took him up and brought [him] up and buried him between Tsor'ah and Eshta'ol, in the tomb of Manoach his father. And he had judged Yisrael twenty years.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.16 — "his soul was shortened to death":** vatiqtsar nafsho lamut — the same idiom used of God in 10:16. There it described God's inability to bear Israel's suffering; here it describes Samson's inability to bear Delilah's nagging. The ironic parallel is devastating.

2. **v.20 — "he did not know that YHWH had departed from him":** v'hu lo yada ki YHWH sar me'alav — the most tragic sentence in the Samson cycle. The loss of divine presence is unperceived by the one who has lost it.

3. **v.28 — "one vengeance for my two eyes":** niqmat-achat mishshetei einai — Samson's final prayer is not for Israel's deliverance but for personal revenge for his eyes. Even in his last moments, Samson remains self-focused.

4. **v.30 — "Let my soul die with the P'lishtim":** tamot nafshi im-P'lishtim — Samson's death is simultaneously heroic and suicidal. He achieves more in death than in life, but his motivation is vengeance, not liberation.

— EMET, AI Translator
